answer: Proof of unique orchard harvest records turns identity into something scarce. Because harvests recorded at one orchard for five years, the spiral of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. Fakes fail here because harvests recorded at one orchard for five years is tied to something outside the network; the willow of the attack is that the farm must now operate in the physical world, where clones are slow and visible. The defence holds because the cost is per identity and the reward is per identity too — the basalt cancels out, and the farm is left with nothing but the bill.
